newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won at 6-year low, central bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won at 6-year low, central bank intervenes.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea on Wednesday intervened to support the won as it slid to a new six-year low following heavy demand for U.S. dollars by importers, traders said.
It is the lowest level for the won since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
"It looks like the central bank began to sell dollars when the won fell to a new six-year low of 830.30," said a dealer with a domestic bank.
The won previously hit a six-year low of 830.00 on September 16.
By 0145 GMT the won was trading at 829.70, steady from the opening. Dealers said they expected the currency to move between 827.00 and 830.00 in the afternoon.
"The U.S. dollar is rising on import deals and bullish sentiment," one local dealer said.
